A `.meta.json` file never creates an instance. It only changes an instance that Rojo already makes from a sibling with the same name, such as `Ping.luau` or a `Ping/` directory. There's nothing called `Ping` in that folder, so Rojo has nothing to apply the meta to and ignores it. In Studio, `Remotes` syncs as an empty Folder.

**Fix:** rename the file to `src/shared/Foo/Remotes/Ping.model.json` and keep the same content:

```json
{"className": "RemoteEvent"}
```

A `.model.json` file creates the instance, and Rojo takes the name `Ping` from the filename. Don't add `name` or `children` to a `.meta.json` file to work around this. The pre-commit hook blocks both keys.

The project's fix is to regenerate the key. It doesn't try to debug the 401. This is documented in `wiki/reference/open-cloud.md:11`:

1. Open https://create.roblox.com/dashboard/credentials → **API Keys**.
2. Click the existing key → **Regenerate**, or create a new key with the `asset:write` scope.
3. In `.env`, replace the old line with `ROBLOX_OPEN_CLOUD_API_KEY=<new value>`.
4. Re-run the call that failed.

The wiki says the root cause isn't worth chasing. The value the dashboard gives you seems to stop working after a short time, even when the key is set to never expire. So you regenerate it whenever it fails.

Never commit the key. Since you're issuing a new one anyway, give it only the scope it needs.

Use the thumbnail URL instead:

```
rbxthumb://type=Asset&id=<id>&w=420&h=420
```

The project tested this and recorded it in `wiki/reference/open-cloud.md:23`. When a Decal is uploaded through Open Cloud (`POST /assets/v1/assets`, `assetType="Decal"`), its id never loads as `rbxassetid://<id>`. `IsLoaded` stays false, even after `PreloadAsync` and minutes of waiting. The probable cause is that the Decal record exists right away, but the Image asset behind it is slow to become reachable or never does. `rbxthumb://` reads the Decal directly, so it works.

- `w`/`h` set the size that gets fetched. 420 works well for HUD icons.
- Images uploaded through Studio's Asset Manager go through a different pipeline, and `rbxassetid://` works fine for those.

No, the game isn't running at 15 fps. 66.668 ms is exactly 1/15 s. That's the frame-pacing target Studio uses when its window isn't focused, not a real measurement. When this was checked on 2026-08-20, `RenderAverage` read exactly 66.668 ms while `RenderThreadAverage` read about 2.4 ms. As a rule, a time that lands exactly on 1/N seconds is pacing.

To measure render cost, use per-frame **counts**, because pacing and window focus don't change them:
- **Draw counts:** `Stats.RenderBreakdown` children (`Opaque`, `Transparent`, `UI`, `Particles`…). `:GetValueString()` returns something like `"7598 tris, 121 draws"`.
- **Batch counts:** `Stats.FrameRateManager` gives `Batches`, `Indices` and `MaterialChanges`.
- **Fix the quality level** with `RenderSettings.QualityLevel = Level21`. Set it back to `Automatic` afterwards, because it's a persistent Studio setting.

This is documented in `wiki/reference/roblox-engine.md:21`.

`execute_luau` runs in its own Luau context. When you call `require()` there, you get a fresh copy of `SpellRegistry`, separate from the one the game's scripts loaded, so your edit only changed your private copy. One sign of this: `[SpellRegistry] Loaded` prints a second time. Module singletons and module-local BindableEvents don't cross that boundary either.

What does cross is DataModel state: attributes, Instances and Instance signals.

- **To drive gameplay:** add a hook to a dev harness that runs when an attribute is set and then clears it, like `workspace:SetAttribute("DevFillMana", n)` in `DevDebug.client.luau`. From MCP, you only set the attribute.
- **To observe results:** set up a `DescendantAdded` observer before you act, and have it record counts into attributes.

The details are in `wiki/reference/studio-mcp.md:13`.

Call **`VfxBroadcast.playAt`** with the world position. For a skill effect, use the `SkillVisuals` primitive that wraps it instead. The routing between the two lives in `SkillVisuals`, not at the call site.

Don't call `spawnEffect` from the server. Players only see what their own client draws, so `VfxBroadcast` sends the effect to every client and each client renders it (`docs/agents/vfx-sfx.md:18`). For an effect attached to an instance, use `playOn`. For a ring burst, use `shockwave`.

**Why:** A `.meta.json` file can only change an instance that Rojo is already creating from a matching sibling, such as `Ping.luau` or a `Ping/` directory. Nothing named `Ping` exists in that folder, so `Ping.meta.json` has nothing to attach to. Rojo ignores it and creates no instance.

**Fix:** Rename it to `src/shared/Foo/Remotes/Ping.model.json` and keep the same content:

```json
{"className": "RemoteEvent"}
```

A `.model.json` file creates its own instance, and it must declare `className`. Rojo will now create `Remotes` as a Folder with a `Ping` RemoteEvent inside it. Don't add `name` or `children` to a `.meta.json` to work around this. The pre-commit hook rejects both keys.

If you're adding several hand-authored remotes and want Studio-side children kept, also add `Remotes/init.meta.json` with `{"className": "Folder", "ignoreUnknownInstances": true}`.
